Label: Government responsibility for jobs and living standards
Current_evidence_note: Government jobs/living standards responsibility: original high values prefer individual responsibility. The 2008 OLD half-sample uses the comparable version; NEW uses an alternative version.

Label: Aid to Black people
Current_evidence_note: The 2012 Sources entry is absent despite observed CDF values. Historical wording differences in 1986/1988 do not alone establish poor comparability in 2004-2024. Source provenance requires further single-wave verification.

Label: Legal availability of abortion
Current_evidence_note: Four ordered substantive abortion categories; original high values are more permissive. In 2008 NEW uses branching questions; in 2016 web cases lack the Other option.

Label: Government services and spending
Current_evidence_note: General government services/spending explicitly mentions health and education. The 2004 CDF uses the pre-election version. In 2008 NEW uses a branching series.

Label: Defence spending
Current_evidence_note: The official note says the 2012 seven-point scale is incomparable, not that the question was never administered. This CDF field has no substantive 2012 observations. In 2008 NEW uses a branching series.

Label: Federal spending on dealing with crime
Current_evidence_note: Crime spending: codes 1/2/3; code 3 includes cut out entirely before 2012. The prior 2008 source repair is documented in ANES_SOURCE_MAPPING_EVIDENCE_G02B.csv; respondent-level source matching is not rerun here.

Label: Federal spending on public schools
Current_evidence_note: Public-school spending: codes 1/2/3; code 3 includes cut out entirely before 2012. Question order varies across years according to the common spending notes.

Label: Federal spending on welfare programmes
Current_evidence_note: Welfare-programme spending, not the separate aid-to-the-poor item. Codes 1/2/3; code 3 includes cut out entirely before 2012.

Label: Federal spending on the environment
Current_evidence_note: The official Question block explicitly lists 2012: fedspend_enviro although Sources omits the year. The 2004 field is entirely system missing. Code 7 remains a substantive volunteered response; it is not merged or discarded.

Label: Federal spending on Social Security
Current_evidence_note: All five primary years have documented sources and substantive observations. Code 7 is a separate substantive volunteered response. Historical exclusion rationale is not recovered; the current scope disposition is preserved without claiming data infeasibility.

Label: Preferred immigration level
Current_evidence_note: The title says 4-category but one is DK: substantive codes are only 1/3/5. Prior 2024 source repair uses V242227; its earlier respondent-level matching is not repeated in this audit.

Label: Perceived likelihood that immigration takes jobs
Current_evidence_note: Higher original values mean lower perceived immigration employment threat. The first listed source year is 2004, constraining the common start of this fixed nine-node set.

Label: Party identification
Current_evidence_note: A constructed seven-category party-identification measure with sources in all six years. Its exclusion concerns policy-versus-identity scope, not data unavailability.

Label: Liberal-conservative self-placement
Current_evidence_note: Liberal-conservative self-placement is outside the selected policy-item scope. The 2012 web questionnaire omitted the haven't-thought option; code 9 is non-substantive even when printed under Valid.

Label: Importance of religion
Current_evidence_note: CDF substantive coding is 1/2 throughout these years. The 2020 source question's five categories were officially collapsed into the existing binary CDF coding. It is not a policy attitude; binary coding alone is not a validity failure.
